text:
clara_cs: Quick triage note from onboarding with FluxForge. They rotated keys and then their CI runners (GitHub Actions) kicked off hundreds of parallel jobs building test artifacts; within 30s they saw a flurry of 429s and a handful of 401s. Happened during a canary ramp.

mike_sdk: do we know whether the CI jobs are using ephemeral tokens or a long-lived service key?

clara_cs: ephemeral, TTL=45s. Each job requests a token just before running tests. Their infra also uses IP rotation via ephemeral runners, so auth sees lots of new source IPs. Logs they pasted show `auth.issue` spikes and many short `429` with missing `Retry-After`.

rory_support: that combination (short TTL + many parallel refreshes + IP churn) smells like a token stampede + anti-abuse heuristics kicking in. We should slow-refresh and leader-elect per pipeline run.

mike_sdk: propose immediate client change: clamp refresh window and add single-refresh leader per repo-run. Example for node CI agent: ```js
// in CI bootstrap
const sdk = new RedwoodSDK({
  tokenRefresh: { leaderElection: true, refreshWindowSec: 20, maxConcurrentRefreshes: 1 },
  retry: { baseMs: 500, maxMs: 5000, jitter: true, maxAttempts: 6, respectRetryAfter: true }
});
```

dina_eng: two infra notes: 1) our auth service applies a short-term per-tenant IP newness throttle to mitigate credential stuffing; 2) missing `Retry-After` on some 429s is from an upstream proxy that strips headers when under load. We should correlate proxy CPU + auth throttle events.

clara_cs: FluxForge cannot change GitHub Actions easily across many repos this week. They asked for a temporary throughput bump during their onboarding window.

onboard-bot: Quota change requested by rory_support for tenant flux-88: +70% burst for 5 hours (audit-id: q-2026-2001).

ava_sales: flagging renewal owner  bad first-run experience could impact conversion. If >12h mitigation needed we'll offer an onboarding eng session.

mike_sdk: short-term mitigation checklist for customer: 1) create a small leader script that elects one job per workflow to fetch/lease token and write to workspace; 2) add exponential jittered backoff for retries; 3) if possible increase ephemeral TTL to 90s during ramp. I'll paste a tiny leader script snippet into KB.

clara_cs: pasted log excerpt they shared: ```
AUTH_ISSUE tenant=flux-88 requester=gha-runner-12 ip=3.103.12.43 -> issued token ttl=45
AUTH_ISSUE tenant=flux-88 requester=gha-runner-53 ip=18.197.4.2 -> issued token ttl=45
429 tenant=flux-88 -> rate_limited (no Retry-After)
```

dina_eng: I'll open INF-3990 to add metrics: `tenant.flux-88.auth_issues`, `auth.ip_newness_throttle_events`, and `proxy.strip_429_headers` so we can validate.

mike_sdk: leader script example (bash) for their CI: ```bash
# elect a leader job via workspace lock file
if mkdir -p /tmp/ci-lock-{{workflow_id}} && ln -s $$ /tmp/ci-lock-{{workflow_id}}/leader; then
  # this job is leader: fetch token once and write to shared workspace
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/auth/lease -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_KEY" -o token.json
fi
# other jobs poll for token.json with backoff
```

rory_support: I applied the temporary quota bump (onboard-bot confirmed). Customer accepted a 5-hour window.

ava_sales: noted. I'll offer a follow-up call with an onboarding engineer if needed after the window.

dina_eng: ticket INF-3990 created. Adding triage tags `auth`, `proxy`, `tenant=flux-88`.

clara_cs: I'll send FluxForge a short one-pager with the leader pattern, SDK snippet and a recommended monitoring checklist. Scheduling a 20-min watch at 07:00 UTC tomorrow to observe CI runs.

mike_sdk: will add the leader script + SDK defaults to our CI onboarding KB and recommend default TTL=90s for heavy parallel CI use-cases.

clara_cs: thanks all, moving this to follow-up after the watch session. :thumbsup:
